[rclone](https://rclone.org/) is a command-line program to manage files
on cloud storage — sometimes described as "rsync for cloud storage." It
talks to 70+ storage backends (S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive,
Backblaze B2, SFTP, and plain local disk, among many others) through one
consistent command set.

## Overview

Every storage backend rclone talks to is configured as a **remote** — a
named config entry you reference as `remote:path`, the same way you'd
reference a local path. Once a remote is set up, the same commands
(`copy`, `sync`, `ls`, ...) work identically whether the other side is
S3, Google Drive, or another machine over SFTP.

## Quick start

This assumes rclone is already installed — see [Installation](installation.qmd).

```bash
rclone config                       # interactive: set up a remote, e.g. "myremote"
rclone lsd myremote:                 # list directories at the remote's root
rclone copy /local/path myremote:backup/   # copy local -> remote, never deletes anything
rclone sync /local/path myremote:backup/   # make remote match local exactly (can delete on the remote side)
```

See [Command reference](reference.md) for the rest of the essentials,
and [Concepts](design.md) for what a "remote" actually is and how the
config file works.
